info.title: SoloW API
info.description: tRPC-over-HTTP surface for the core-program loop (Decision 0011).

get.summary: The signed-in user's provider login on each connected Integration. Mappings whose Integration has been disconnected are not listed.

post.summary: State the signed-in user's login on one Integration's provider — what `assignee:@me` resolves to on the projects that Integration owns. Stated rather than read from the token: the token is the Workspace's, so it names whoever issued it.
Forget the signed-in user's login on one Integration. `@me` then matches nothing on that Integration's projects, and the table says the mapping is missing.

get.summary: What `@me` resolves to on one Project — the signed-in user's login on the provider that Project belongs to. `login` is null when no mapping has been stated, which the table states rather than rendering as an empty result.
List Issues in the Workspace, newest first. An Issue is either imported from a connected GitHub/GitLab repository or created directly.
Fetch one Issue by id, including how many Tasks sit under it.
Every distinct label in use on the Workspace's Issues, sorted — the vocabulary the list filter offers.
Every label the linked Repositories define, with the colour its provider gives it. Null where the provider reports none.

post.summary: Set an Issue's status by hand, overriding the one derived from its Tasks, or pass `status: null` to follow the Tasks again. Closing is refused while Tasks are still active unless `force` is set.
Create a local Issue directly, without importing it from a provider.
Edit an Issue's title, description or labels. Title/description are refused for an Issue imported from a provider — they are owned by the source.

get.summary: Count what a force delete of this Issue would destroy — Tasks, sessions and active worktrees — so the confirmation can state it.

post.summary: Delete an Issue. Refused while it still has Tasks unless `force` is set, which stops any running Task and then deletes the Issue together with its Tasks, sessions and worktree records.

get.summary: One imported Issue read live from its provider, with the labels, people and milestones that provider will accept — and which fields it will accept a change to at all.

post.summary: Change an imported Issue on the provider that owns it. A field absent from the request is not changed; the answer is what the provider now holds, never what was sent.
Create an Issue on the connected provider (GitHub/GitLab) and mirror it back.

get.summary: The comments on one imported Issue, oldest first, read live from its provider. A provider's activity entries are not comments and are not included.

post.summary: Post a comment on an imported Issue. Answers with the whole thread as the provider now holds it, never with the text that was sent.

get.summary: Every integration provider this build has a driver for, with the capabilities it offers and the fields its connect form needs. Optionally narrowed to providers offering one capability.

post.summary: Connect a GitHub or GitLab account using a stored Personal Access Token Secret. The token is verified against the provider before the Integration is recorded, then every Repository the token can see is imported automatically (capped; partial failures are reported per Repository, not raised as a mutation error), each with its own Issues.

get.summary: List connected GitHub/GitLab Integrations.

post.summary: Disconnect an Integration. Its Repositories are unlinked and the branches and change requests synced from it are removed, since nothing can refresh them once the credential is gone. Imported Issues are kept and detached — Tasks point at them.

get.summary: List the repositories this Integration's token can actually see, flagging the ones already linked. Backs the link picker so a repository is chosen from real options rather than typed.

post.summary: Import a repository from an Integration, creating the Repository already bound to it and then importing its Issues automatically. Records the provider's clone URL; the orchestrator clones it the first time a Task needs it. Importing the same repository twice returns the existing Repository.

get.summary: Preview the issues on a linked Repository's provider, flagging which have already been imported.

post.summary: Import selected external issues as SoloW Issues. Idempotent per Repository — re-importing the same ids is a visible no-op, not a duplicate.
Refresh a linked Repository's change requests (pull/merge requests) and branches from its provider. On-demand pull; SoloW never creates or modifies anything on the provider here.

get.summary: List issued MCP tokens as metadata only — label, scope, prefix, last use, revocation. Token values are never returned by a read.

post.summary: Issue a scoped MCP token. The value is returned exactly once, in this response, and is not recoverable afterwards.
Revoke an MCP token. Takes effect on the token's next request; the row is kept so the audit trail survives.

get.summary: Read the signed-in user's arrangement of a contributed surface. Returns the default arrangement when nothing is saved.

post.summary: Save the signed-in user's arrangement of a contributed surface — the complete order and hidden list, not a delta.

get.summary: Read the signed-in user's Task page split — the width of the changes column and whether it is folded. Returns the default when nothing is saved.

post.summary: Save the signed-in user's Task page split.

Create a Task under an Issue, binding an Agent Profile, an Executor Profile, and one or more Repositories — each with its own base ref and checkout branch. Creates it in the backlog; it does not start an agent — use task.launch for that.

Replace the whole set of Repositories a Task works in, each with its own base ref and checkout branch. Refused once the Task has left the backlog or ready states, because its worktrees are already live.

get.summary: List Tasks on the board, optionally filtered by Issue or lifecycle state.
Fetch one Task by id, including its current state and result branch.

post.summary: Start an agent on a ready Task in its own isolated worktree. Rate limited, and refused if the Agent Profile is already at its concurrency cap. The run ends at a human review gate — it never merges on its own.
Move a Task to another lifecycle state. Illegal transitions are refused by the state machine rather than applied.
Open the review gate on a Task whose agent has declared it finished. Refused when no declaration has been made — the gate is for judging finished work, not work still in progress.
Re-run a failed or parked Task in a fresh Session, clearing the previous failure reason.

get.summary: List blocked_by dependencies — for one Task, or for every Task in the Workspace when no id is given. Each edge carries the blocking Task's title and current state, so a caller can see what is still outstanding.

post.summary: Declare that a Task is blocked by another Task in the same Workspace. Refused if the edge would create a cycle, naming the offending path. Re-declaring an existing dependency is a no-op.
Withdraw a blocked_by dependency between two Tasks, returning the Task's remaining dependencies.

get.summary: Count what deleting this Task would destroy — sessions, active worktrees, and the Tasks currently blocked by it.

post.summary: Delete a Task with its sessions, reviews and worktree records. A running Task is stopped first. Refused while other Tasks are blocked by it unless `force` is set, which drops those edges too.
Create an Agent Profile: which catalog agent to run, its billing/auth mode, the Secret holding its credential, and its concurrency cap.

get.summary: List Agent Profiles available to bind to a Task, with how many Tasks, Workflow Steps and Sessions each is used by.

post.summary: Edit an Agent Profile's name, concurrency cap or permission mode. The agent it runs and the credential it runs on are fixed at creation — changing those would rewrite what its finished runs meant.
Delete an Agent Profile. Refused while a Task, a Workflow Step, or a Session's usage record still references it.
Test an Agent Profile: launch its agent with its credential, complete the protocol handshake, and report whether it works and what models and modes it advertises.

get.summary: List the agents this Workspace can run — the catalog an Agent Profile points at.

post.summary: Declare a new agent this Workspace can run: which protocol it speaks, the command that starts it, and the two environment variables billing integrity depends on.
Create an Executor Profile — where an agent runs, with per-kind typed configuration. Credentials are given as Secret references, never inline values.
Update an Executor Profile's name or its per-kind configuration.

get.summary: List Executor Profiles available to bind to a Task.
Every planning Project mirrored in this Workspace.
One Project with its field set — the columns, their types, and which of them this provider cannot hold.
One page of a Project's rows, values already read back against their fields' types.
Every row of a Project, paged internally up to a ceiling. `truncated` says when the ceiling was reached — a rollup or a filter computed over part of a project must be able to say so.
Projects this Workspace's tokens can see, across every integration that declares the capability. One unreachable host costs its own projects and nothing else.

post.summary: Import a project: create whatever structure the provider needs to hold one (scoped labels on GitLab; nothing on GitHub), pull every issue of its repositories, then scan every page of the project itself. Reports what it created, so a write made without a confirmation step is at least visible afterwards.
Create a local Project — a container SoloW owns outright, with no provider board behind it. Its membership is decided by which Repositories are registered under it, not by a sync.

get.summary: The Repositories registered under a Project, and how many Issues each currently contributes. Empty on a mirrored Project — its membership comes from a sync, not this list.

post.summary: Register a Repository under a local Project. Every Issue it already holds is attached immediately, and every Issue it gets later arrives the same way. Refused on a mirrored Project.
Remove a Repository from a local Project. Every project item and value that Repository's Issues held in this Project is removed with it; the Issues and the Repository itself are untouched.
Write one field value to the provider and return what the provider now holds — not what was sent. Refused for a field the provider cannot hold.
Pull the next page of a Project's mirror. Rows whose Issue has not been ingested yet are skipped and counted, not invented.
Re-read every page of a Project, connecting the repositories its rows need. The repair path for a mirror that finished a sync holding nothing.

get.summary: The Project that holds one Issue, or null when no Project does. Lets a Task or Issue page reached by its own flat route link back into the Project it belongs to.
The saved views of one Project — the tab strip, in the order the team put it in. A view is a configuration; it carries no items.

post.summary: Add a tab, at the end of the strip. Its configuration is a filter, a grouping, a sort, a layout and a column set — never a copy of the rows.
Rename a view, reconfigure it, or both. An omitted half is left alone rather than overwritten from a stale copy.
Put the tab strip in the order given. The whole strip at once, so two people dragging tabs cannot interleave into an order neither chose.
Delete a saved view. The rows it selected are the Project's and stay — a tab is a question, not the answer.
Create an Epic in a group on the connected provider. Refused with a stated reason on a provider that has no epics; the answer is the epic the provider stored, never what was sent.

get.summary: The groups this connection can create an epic in — a pick rather than a typed guess. Empty on a provider without epics is not the answer; it is refused with the reason.
The epics already in a group, read live from the provider — what an Issue can be created under.

post.summary: Delete a Project — local or mirrored — from SoloW's own database: its saved views, fields, values and items. Its Issues are kept and become unassigned; a mirrored Project's provider is never touched.
Connect a Git repository to the Workspace, by local path or remote URL, so Tasks can run against it.

get.summary: List connected Repositories, including which Integration each is linked to.

post.summary: Replace the allowlist of files copied from the Repository into every new worktree, such as a .env the agent needs to run the test suite.

get.summary: Fetch a linked Repository's real labels from its GitHub/GitLab Integration, for the Issue label picker.
Fetch the users a linked Repository's GitHub/GitLab Integration can assign an Issue to, for the assignee picker.
Fetch a linked Repository's milestones from its GitHub/GitLab Integration, for the Issue milestone picker.
Fetch the issue types a linked Repository's provider offers, for the Issue type picker. Empty where the provider has no such vocabulary.

post.summary: Create SoloW's default label taxonomy (type/, prio/, size/, status/, area/) on a linked Repository's GitHub/GitLab, leaving any label it already has untouched.
Record the human decision on a Session's diff: approve (commit), reject (discard), or request_changes (resume the agent with feedback). This is the review gate — nothing is integrated without it.
Delete a Secret. Refused while an Integration or Agent Profile still references it.

get.summary: List every agent Session recorded for a Task, newest first.

Fetch one Session with its event log — minus any range a compaction summary stands in for, which session.eventRange reads back — the diff captured at the review gate for each Repository the Task works in, and any recorded decision.
Read the events inside one closed seq range of a Session's log — what a compaction summary stands in for.
Mint a content-addressed fork cursor for a Session, at a given seq or at the head of its log.
Read the events recorded after a fork cursor, refusing a cursor whose hash no longer matches the log.
List this Workspace's Workflows — repeatable pipelines of Steps, each Step run by its own Agent Profile. Returns the definition version and how many Steps each has, not the Steps themselves.
Read one Workflow with its Steps, in pipeline order.

post.summary: Create an empty Workflow. Steps are added afterwards with workflow.addStep; a Workflow with no Steps cannot be attached to a Task.
Rename a Workflow, and optionally replace its description.
Delete a Workflow and its Steps. Refused while any Task still follows it, so no Task is left with a cursor pointing at nothing.

Add a Step to a Workflow, bound to an Agent Profile with its own prompt template and gate rule. Appends unless afterStepId names the Step it should follow; inserting in the middle writes one row and reorders nothing.
Change a Step's name, Agent Profile, prompt template, gate or advance rule. Bumps the Workflow's definition version, so an attached Task reports the drift.

Move a Step between the two Steps it should sit between; either may be null for the ends of the list. Refused if those two are not adjacent any more, which means the caller was looking at a stale order.
Remove a Step from a Workflow. Refused while a Task's cursor sits on it, because that Task would then be unable to resume.

Put a Task on a Workflow, at its first Step, recording the definition version in force. Refused once the Task has left backlog or ready, and refused once it has begun a pipeline — a cursor that has moved, a handoff, or a spent approval — so re-attaching cannot silently discard work already done.

Take a Task off its Workflow, clearing its step cursor and carried handoff. Refused for a Task that follows no Workflow, and for one that has left backlog or ready — detaching mid-run would throw away the durable cursor and defeat the guards that refuse to delete a Step a run is on.

get.summary: Where a Task is in its Workflow: the current Step with its Agent Profile, the whole Step list, the carried handoff, and the brief the current Step's agent should be given.

post.summary: Accept the Workflow definition as it now stands for one Task, clearing its drift warning. The step cursor is untouched — this records that a person read what changed underneath the run and chose to carry on.

Report that a Task's current Step finished, moving it to the next Step and carrying the handoff. fromStepId names the Step the caller believes it is finishing, so a redelivered call is refused rather than skipping a Step. The same Task is moved; no new Task is created. The last Step reports completed only once a human approval has been recorded that no earlier gate already spent, whatever the Step's gate says.

get.summary: The caller's own Workspace: id, name and when it was created.

post.summary: Rename the caller's own Workspace.

get.summary: What this Workspace still needs before it can run anything — a credential, an Agent Profile, an Executor, a Repository and the core loop — derived from what it actually has.
